key_insight: A causal digital-twin model stratified by HPV status estimated who with head and neck cancer may gain more survival benefit from chemoradiotherapy versus radiotherapy alone.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more personalized treatment selection by identifying patients most likely to benefit from adding chemotherapy, while avoiding one-size-fits-all decisions.
method: Used the public RADCURE cohort (n=3,346) and split patients by HPV status.
Learned each group’s minimal causal feature set with Bayesian-network Markov Blanket discovery around 2-year survival.
Estimated individualized treatment effects with a causal forest in a double machine learning framework and applied overlap restrictions.
evidence_signal: In HPV-negative disease, the model showed solid test performance (AUC 0.72, C-index 0.81) and a modest positive average treatment effect favoring chemoradiotherapy; decision-curve analysis suggested higher net benefit for a selective-CRT strategy.
watch_item: HPV-positive results showed greater heterogeneity but also reduced overlap and higher uncertainty, so prospective validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: HPV-Stratified Causal Digital Twins for Personalized Survival Benefit Estimation in Head and Neck Cancer
